Current internal state:
- View A: attention is almost entirely on the upper location, represented as a green square (color: green ≈1.0; shape: square ≈1.0) with selection probability 0.99947. Recoverability for that item is ~0.70 now, ~0.50 after one step, ~0.36 after two steps. The right location is represented as a red cross (red ≈0.9998; cross ≈1.0) but has negligible current selection (0.00041) and recoverability ~0.57→0.42→0.29. The lower location is undifferentiated (flat color and shape distribution) with very low selection and very low recoverability (~0.03). The left is a blue circle (blue ≈1.0; circle ≈1.0) with very low selection and moderate recoverability (~0.22→0.16→0.12).
- View B: attention is almost entirely on the left location, represented as a red circle (red=1.0; circle=1.0) with selection probability 0.99997 and recoverability ~0.68→0.48→0.34. Other B locations are represented (upper: green triangle; right: yellow square; lower: blue, mostly cross) but have negligible current selection and lower recoverability.

How redirection would change allocation (predicted):
- In A, command "upper" keeps selection on upper (~0.99992); "right" would move selection to the right (~0.99978); "lower" to lower (~0.99972); "left" to left (~0.99987).
- In B, commands largely keep or shift to specific locations: commanding upper/right/lower/left leads to high predicted selection probabilities for the indicated targets in B (e.g., many commands predict selection of lower or upper depending on command; left is currently dominant unless a command targets another location).

These are internal, fallible predictions of what the system would select and how recoverable each item is now and after one or two steps.
